title: Use-case alignment + deployment pathways scoping - ScoutWorks POC
summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria for clinical-notes summarization, workload sizing (concurrency and RPS), benchmark plan, and timeline. Primary decision points: latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, and data residency/compliance needs. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and agreed on a 4-week pilot: 2-week bench + 2-week model-integration with a possible Dedicated trial depending on benchmarks.
topics: Workload sizing: qps/rps, concurrency, KV cache patterns
Benchmarks: test harness, sample prompt set, tokenization
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (tradeoffs)
action_items: Ava Chen - Share POC pricing template and pilot SOW - 2026-10-16
Diego Marquez - Provide benchmark harness (script + runner) and sample load profile - 2026-10-19
Lena Ortiz - Share 200 sample clinical notes and priority prompt set (anonymized) - 2026-10-18
Priya Singh - Send security questionnaire and confirmation of required encryption-at-rest controls - 2026-10-17
Marcus Bell - Provide target throughput (RPS) & expected concurrency for peak hour - 2026-10-16
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline latency/cost benchmark on hosted with HD-quant model (2 business days)
Customer to provide anonymized sample dataset and target SLAs
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) after baseline results to decide Dedicated pilot
Exchange security docs and schedule compliance review call if Dedicated/Private is required
questions: What is acceptable p50/p95 latency for triage flow?
Are there strict data residency rules requiring on-prem or VPC?
What is the monthly token budget that would shift economics toward Dedicated?
Is there a need for KMS/HSM integration for keys?
header: Date: 2026-10-14 15:30 UTC | Duration: 55m | Redwood AE+SE (Ava, Diego) | Customer: ScoutWorks (Lena, Marcus, Priya)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE on this account. Diego, our SE, is here as well. Can you quick intro from ScoutWorks?
[00:10] Lena: Yeah hi I'm Lena, Head of ML at ScoutWorks. We own the clinical notes summarization project. Marcus is on platform, Priya handles security.
[00:18] Marcus: Morning, thanks.
[00:20] Diego: Nice to meet you all. Today we'd like to align on success criteria and pick a path - hosted, dedicated, or private - for the POC.
[00:30] Priya: Quick note — security constraints might push us toward VPC/on-prem, but we want to see the numbers first.
[00:38] Ava: Totally. Let's start with goals: what does a successful POC look like for you, Lena?
[00:45] Lena: Success is twofold — first, latency for the triage assistant needs to be under ~250ms p50, p95 under 700ms ideally. Second is quality: label-level F1 > 0.82 on our eval prompts. Third is economics — cost per 1k tokens needs to be below our current AWS-hosted baseline.
[01:10] Diego: Good, we can measure p50/p95 and token cost. When you say AWS baseline, can you give ballpark monthly tokens?
[01:17] Lena: Right now we see roughly 40M tokens/month for triage plus spikes. That could grow.
[01:24] Marcus: Peak concurrency is the tricky part — during shift changes we see bursts up to 180 concurrent requests.
[01:30] Ava: That helps. For sizing, Diego, any initial thoughts?
[01:34] Diego: With 180 concurrency and 40M tokens, we typically look at Dedicated or a well-configured hosted plan with autoscaling. The Hosted plan handles variability well, but Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency and cost per token if the commit is high.
[01:50] Marcus: And Private would be for our compliance team but it's heavier to set up.
[01:55] Priya: Yes, we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, and KMS integration. Data residency: data must stay in EU region for certain subsets.
[02:05] Ava: Redwood supports region pinning, KMS and SOC2. For Private we can offer our VPC control plane option or an on-prem bundle. Diego, talk benchmarks and KV cache implications.
[02:15] Diego: Sure. For summarization, we expect repeated prefixes — good candidate for prefix/KV caching. That reduces per-token compute when the same patient context repeats. Our benchmark harness will simulate your prompt set and cache-hit ratios. We'll run three profiles: cold (no cache), warm (30% cache hit), and hot (60%+).
[02:40] Lena: Our real traffic is close to warm; many clinicians reuse templates. Also we have interactive sessions where latency matters more.
[02:48] Diego: Then metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also capture failure modes — cold start CPU/GPU spin-up and any OOMs.
[03:05] Marcus: On networking — if we choose Private, we'll need bandwidth planning. Our on-prem infra has limited egress to public clouds.
[03:12] Priya: Also need to confirm audit logging: we need immutable logs for inference requests for 90 days.
[03:20] Ava: We'll include audit log retention options in the SOW. Diego, how long to run initial hosted benchmark?
[03:26] Diego: Baseline run can be done in 48 hours once we get the sample prompts and tokenization profile. We'll provide the harness and a dockerized runner.
[03:35] Lena: We'll share 200 anonymized notes and identify priorities.
[03:40] Marcus: On cost, what tipping point makes Dedicated cheaper?
[03:45] Diego: Typically at sustained heavy usage — around 30–40M tokens/month with consistent throughput, Dedicated starts to beat hosted per-token cost, especially if you allow quantization and reduced precision models. But there's an upfront commit and instance allocation.
[04:00] Priya: Quantization — our compliance team is worried about model determinism and hallucinations when using quantized models.
[04:07] Diego: Understandable. We'll run quality regressions in the benchmark harness, comparing fp16 vs int8/int4 quantized variants. Redwood Optimize can suggest the best quantization profile per workload.
[04:20] Ava: Also decision factor: how fast we can get you into a pilot. Hosted is fastest — we can be running benchmarks in days. Dedicated requires capacity provisioning which takes 2–3 weeks typically. Private on-prem could be 6–10 weeks depending on procurement.
[04:38] Lena: Timeline wise we want results quickly. So probably hosted bench first then decide.
[04:42] Marcus: Agreed — but if the benchmarks show we need isolation we might push for a Dedicated trial.
[04:47] Priya: One more — encryption keys. We need BYOK (bring your own key) support.
[04:51] Diego: We support KMS integrations and can do customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports KMS with additional controls — we'll detail this in the security doc.
[04:59] Ava: I'll send the security pack. Marcus — can you confirm typical payload sizes and tokenization expectations?
[05:05] Marcus: Typical note is 350–600 tokens post-tokenize, but we have longer discharge summaries up to 2k tokens once in a while.
[05:14] Diego: Good to know. That affects memory/KV cache sizing. For larger sequences we might pick a model variant with better long context performance.
[05:24] Lena: For quality evals, we have an internal set of 1,000 labeled examples. We'll give a subset for the benchmark without PHI.
[05:31] Ava: Perfect. Bench plan: Redwood runs hosted baseline (2 days). After we share results, SE deep dive to consider Dedicated trial for 2 weeks with reserved GPUs, if economics and latency benefit. If compliance blocks hosted, we start Private scoping.
[05:46] Priya: If we go Dedicated, can we get audit logs shipped to our SIEM via syslog?
[05:52] Diego: Yes, Dedicated and Private can forward logs, or we can provide S3 exports for hosted.
[05:58] Lena: About SLA — we need 99.9% uptime for the triage service. Is that achievable on Hosted?
[06:05] Ava: Hosted comes with a standard SLA; Dedicated adds stronger latency SLOs and a commercial SLA is part of the reserved contract. We'll include the SLA tiers in the SOW.
[06:15] Marcus: One operational question — what's the rollout path from pilot to production?
[06:20] Diego: Typical path: pilot bench -> dedicated pilot (optional) -> canary rollout on production routes with autoscaling policies and KV cache warmup. We support canary routing per model tag and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[06:33] Priya: Auto-rollback is good. Also need RBAC controls — who can deploy model versions.
[06:38] Ava: RBAC and SSO integration (SAML) included for Enterprise. We'll include role templates in the doc.
[06:45] Marcus: Ok, what do you need from us to start the hosted run?
[06:50] Diego: The anonymized 200-note sample, target concurrency profile (we have 180 but want typical/peak), and tokenization hints. We'll send the harness and a README.
[07:00] Lena: We'll share the data by EOD Tuesday.
[07:04] Ava: Great. I'll follow up with pricing and SOW. Any blockers?
[07:09] Priya: We need the security questionnaire answered before running anything with real data.
[07:13] Ava: Understood — I'll attach the questionnaire in the follow-up.
[07:17] Diego: One last note on benchmarks — we'll surface per-route token breakdown (prompt vs generation), so you can see where costs come from and where caching helps.
[07:26] Marcus: That will be helpful for capacity planning.
[07:29] Lena: Thanks, this feels actionable.
[07:31] Ava: Recap: Redwood runs hosted baseline in 48 hours after data + harness; we evaluate latency/quality/cost; then decide Dedicated pilot if economics favor it or Private if compliance mandates. Next meeting: SE deep dive scheduled after results.
[07:44] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:46] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and next steps.
[07:49] [end of recording]
